import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sum of two squares, a power of 3, and a power of 5

Any integer $n > 1$ can be written as $a^2 + b^2 + 3^c + 5^d$ where $a, b, c, d$ are
nonnegative integers.

Zhi-Wei Sun has offered a \$3,500 prize for the first proof.

*References:*
- [A303656](https://oeis.org/A303656)
- Z.-W. Sun, "Restricted sums of four squares," arXiv preprint:
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05868v10
- Z.-W. Sun, "Refining Lagrange's four-square theorem," Journal of Number Theory:
  http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/RefineFourSquareTh.pdf
- Z.-W. Sun, "Restricted sums of three or four squares":
  http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/Square-sum.pdf
- Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture and variations:
  https://www.aimspress.com/aimspress-data/era/2020/2/PDF/1935-9179_2020_2_589.pdf
-/

namespace OeisA303656

/-- The predicate that `n` can be written as $a^2 + b^2 + 3^c + 5^d$ for nonnegative integers. -/
def A (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c d : ℕ, n = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + 3 ^ c + 5 ^ d

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : A 2 :=
  ⟨0, 0, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : A 3 :=
  ⟨1, 0, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : A 4 :=
  ⟨1, 1, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : A 5 :=
  ⟨0, 1, 1, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_6 : A 6 :=
  ⟨0, 0, 0, 1, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_25 : A 25 :=
  ⟨1, 4, 1, 1, by norm_num⟩

/--
**Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture (A303656)**: Any integer $n > 1$ can be written as the sum of two
squares, a power of 3, and a power of 5.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : A n := by
  sorry

end OeisA303656

findings.description: The reference at lines 35–36, labelled “Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture and variations,” links to an unrelated paper about quadratic residues. This is a citation error, not a defect in the formalized conjecture.
findings.source_evidence: The linked PDF, https://www.aimspress.com/aimspress-data/era/2020/2/PDF/1935-9179_2020_2_589.pdf, identifies itself on page 589 as Fedor Petrov and Zhi-Wei Sun, “Proof of some conjectures involving quadratic residues,” Electronic Research Archive 28(2) (2020), 589–597, DOI 10.3934/era.2020031. Its abstract and introduction concern quadratic residues modulo odd primes, not the 1-3-5 conjecture or A303656.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the unrelated reference or replace its URL with the intended reference. The existing OEIS citation and Sun's arXiv:1701.05868v10, Conjecture 4.1(i), already directly support the Lean statement.

findings.description: The reference at lines 31–32 describes a Journal of Number Theory article, but its PDF link points to Sun's lecture slides with the same title, rather than the journal article.
findings.source_evidence: The first page of http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/RefineFourSquareTh.pdf says “A talk given at” several universities and is dated December 2, 2016; the document consists of 50 slides. The OEIS A303656 reference list identifies the journal article as J. Number Theory 175 (2017), 167–190, DOI 10.1016/j.jnt.2016.11.008.
findings.suggested_fix: Either identify the linked document as Sun's December 2016 lecture slides, or replace the link with https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnt.2016.11.008 for the journal article.

reformulations.difference: OEIS states positivity of the number of representations with a ≤ b; Lean instead asserts existence of a representation, without ordering the two square roots.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any representation can be put in the order a ≤ b by swapping a and b, which preserves a²+b². For fixed n, all four coordinates are bounded by n: a ≤ a² ≤ n, b ≤ b² ≤ n, c < 3^c ≤ n, and d < 5^d ≤ n. Thus the ordered representations form a finite set, whose cardinality is positive exactly when a representation exists. The scratch file proves both A n ↔ positive ordered-representation count and the corresponding universally quantified conjecture equivalence, without using the conjecture.

sources_consulted: OEIS A303656, official data mirror, revision 44 dated May 30, 2026: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A303/A303656.seq
https://arxiv.org/e-print/1701.05868v10 — abstract, Conjecture 4.1(i), Remark 4.1, and bibliography
review.notes: No mathematical statement or definition defects were found; the findings are only minor citation errors. All eight declarations were checked. Sun's Conjecture 4.1(i) explicitly uses nonnegative integers and n > 1, and Remark 4.1 confirms the $3,500 prize. The current OEIS record still presents the claim as conjectural. The main OEIS page was Cloudflare-blocked, so its official data mirror and accessible b-file were used. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully: it confirms all six test proofs, proves ¬ A 0 and ¬ A 1, and proves equivalence with the source's set-equality and integer-domain formulations. Lean witness searches succeed for every 2 ≤ n ≤ 200; an independent ordered-representation count agrees with the OEIS b-file for n = 1..200. No repository files were edited.
